articles.title: Neuronal and glial transcriptional states vary with proximity to tangle-bearing neurons in the human entorhinal cortex
articles.content: More neurons die in Alzheimer's disease than form tangles, and tangle-bearing neurons can persist for decades, so tangles alone cannot explain degeneration. We combined 6,000-plex spatial transcriptomics with PHF1 immunofluorescence (167,176 cells; 9 donors) and imaging mass cytometry (170,195 cells; 62 donors), measuring each cell's distance to the nearest tangle. Tangle-bearing layer 2-3 excitatory neurons were enriched late along a trajectory of increasing microtubule-associated, synaptic and V-ATPase expression, with elevated p62 and K48-ubiquitin. Tangle-free neurons shared more of this state the closer they lay to a tangle, including higher chaperone and autophagy scores, p62 and nuclear size. Nearby glia had higher disease-associated scores, with astrocytes expressing less GFAP. Excitatory, but not inhibitory, neuron loss was greatest in subtypes closest to tangles and cortical depths richest in phosphorylated tau. Selective neuronal vulnerability may reflect not only a neuron's susceptibility to forming a tangle but also where it lies relative to one.

articles.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02499-3

Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

articles.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02489-5

Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.

articles.title: Digital health meets Parkinson’s disease: a bibliometric exploration of wearable sensors research and emerging frontiers (2005–2026)
articles.content: BackgroundWearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies are increasingly used to support objective, longitudinal assessment in Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, the global development, knowledge structure, and emerging research frontiers of this interdisciplinary field remain incompletely mapped.MethodsBibliographic records on wearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies in PD were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus for the period from 1 January 2005 to 2 February 2026. Searches were conducted in title, abstract, and author keyword fields. Microsoft Excel, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix R package were used to analyze publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, citation bursts, historiographic patterns, and source impact.ResultsA total of 3,332 publications were included. Publication output increased rapidly over the study period, particularly after 2019, while 2026 represented an incomplete publication year because the search was conducted on 2 February 2026. The United States (U.S.), China, and European countries constituted the main knowledge-production and collaboration structure. Thematic analyses suggested a gradual shift from engineering validation and objective motor-symptom quantification toward AI-enabled digital biomarkers, remote monitoring, multimodal monitoring, and closed-loop neuromodulation. These patterns reflect research activity and citation structures rather than direct evidence of clinical efficacy.ConclusionThis bibliometric analysis provides science-mapping evidence on the evolution of wearable and sensor-based monitoring technologies in PD. Future work should prioritize standardization, multicenter real-world validation, clinical workflow integration, multimodal data fusion, and cautious evaluation of closed-loop applications.

articles.title: MTDANet: lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery brain–computer interfaces
articles.content: Objective. Motor-imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive route to brain–computer interaction, yet reliable single-trial decoding remains difficult because task-related patterns are weak, nonstationary, and distributed over multiple temporal scales. This study investigates whether a staged local-to-global model can integrate fine temporal–spatial structure with longer-range context without relying on unrestricted self-attention. Approach. We propose MTDANet, an architecture that combines multi-scale temporal–spatial feature extraction, factorized temporal consolidation, and distance-regularized recurrent attention. The model was evaluated on three public MI datasets under subject-specific and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols. Separately initialized models were also trained on P300 and steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) datasets to examine broader architectural applicability. Participant-level paired analyses used two-sided paired tests with within-setting Holm correction. Main results. MTDANet achieved subject-specific accuracies of , , and on brain–computer interface (BCI) Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and BNCI2014_002, respectively. Relative to the highest-mean baseline, the paired improvements were supported after within-setting Holm correction on BCI Competition IV 2a (3.56 percentage points, adjusted ) and 2b (1.62 points, adjusted ). Under LOSO evaluation, the corresponding accuracies were , , and . The 2.08-point BNCI2014_002 difference had a 95% confidence interval of 0.42–3.73 points and an adjusted value of 0.0387. These three comparisons did not remain significant in a broader 56-comparison Holm sensitivity analysis. The P300 and SSVEP models attained the highest observed mean accuracies. Significance. The results provide within-setting evidence for staged local-to-global temporal modeling in offline MI-EEG evaluations.

articles.title: AOR: adaptive orthogonal regression for depression feature selection with incomplete EEG channels
articles.content: Objective. Depression induces severe mental and physical impairments, highlighting the clinical need for rapid and reliable detection. Electroencephalography (EEG) directly reflects neural electrical activity and serves as a promising tool for depression investigation. However, the inherent non-stationarity, redundancy, and noise susceptibility of EEG signals, together with the common issue of incomplete channel data due to electrode loss or severe noise during acquisition, compromise the reliability of diagnostic models. Existing EEG feature selection methods lack adaptability to such incomplete data, leading to distorted feature evaluation and degraded performance. Approach. To address this limitation, an adaptive orthogonal regression (AOR) method is proposed for EEG feature selection for depression detection under incomplete channel conditions. The method integrates three core innovations: embedding missing channel information into the orthogonal regression formulation to mitigate the impact of incomplete channels, incorporating adaptive channel-weighted learning to automatically quantify the relative importance of different channels, and applying global redundancy minimization to eliminate inter-feature redundancy while enhancing discriminability. The optimization problem is solved via Generalized Power Iteration and Augmented Lagrangian Multiplier methods. Main results. AOR was validated on the MODMA and PRED-d003 datasets across 3-channel, 64-channel, and 128-channel configurations under single-modal and multi-modal scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that AOR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various missing ratios and channel configurations. The average cross-subject depression recognition accuracy reaches 92.25% and 95.12% across different missing ratios on the two datasets. Additionally, feature weight analysis reveals that EEG kurtosis consistently exhibits high discriminative power across different configurations. Significance. The proposed AOR method provides a robust and efficient solution for depression feature selection under incomplete EEG channel conditions, offering reliable diagnostic performance in real-world clinical scenarios.

articles.title: Multimodal regulation of neurite extension by extracellular matrix composition and electrical stimulation on aligned collagen fiber scaffolds
articles.content: Objective. Peripheral nerve regeneration is regulated by structural, biochemical, and electrical cues, yet their combined effects on neurite outgrowth remain unclear. In this study, an aligned fibrous scaffold was developed to evaluate how extracellular matrix (ECM) composition and electrical stimulation influence neurite extension and growth cone morphology. Approach. Type I collagen fibers incorporating fibronectin, collagen IV, and laminin I were fabricated by contact drawing. The contact drawn fibers were then consolidated into multifilaments, which were mounted on custom frames for cell culture. Primary dorsal root ganglia (DRG) explants were cultured on the multifilaments, and neurite outgrowth and alignment were quantified as a function of ECM composition. Functional activity was confirmed by patch clamp. High-resolution confocal imaging was performed to assess cytoskeletal organization and growth cone morphology. Electrical stimulation was applied to evaluate interactions between biochemical and bioelectrical cues. Main Results. Collagen multifilament scaffolds promoted a high degree of neurite alignment relative to DRGs cultured on isotropic surfaces. Fibronectin and collagen IV increased neurite length in a concentration-dependent manner, with maximal effects observed at intermediate ligand densities, while laminin I had no significant effect. Combinatorial ECM presentation produced non-additive responses. Electrical stimulation increased neurite length on collagen-only scaffolds but had a reduced effect or no effect with incorporation of additional ECM constituents. Growth cone morphology was altered by ECM composition, with fibronectin-, collagen IV-, and combinatorial scaffolds producing less circular growth cones, despite no significant differences in filopodia number or overall morphology-classification proportions. Significance. Neurite extension and growth cone structure are governed by non-linear interactions between multimodal cues. The scaffold system described here facilitates systematic comparison of multiple regenerative cues to inform the design of material for promoting nerve regeneration.
